page.layout: One page of text, two columns of verse-like lines with a heading and sub-heading above; a short line of verse at the top of the page continues from the previous page; a printed ornament at the foot; a marginal word "Marco" at the right below the text, set apart as a speaker's line; no marginal notes.

main_text.l: Chare nepos, spes una domus, meliore fenestram-
ANna hic Rodolfi iaceo cum prole sepul-
die.Et genus, & faties populo sunt nota: sed vni-
Sat mihi sit mores complacuisse viro:
Quos gemitu probat, & lachrymis, curáque fideli:
Nec patitur famam me moriente mori.
Cocburnum in lucem dedit, & rude pignus alendum-
Sors, vbi maturis accessit robur ab annis,
Sed sibi præferri virtutem irata doloris-
Si numeres annos, cecidit florente iuuenta:

page.notes: Printed text of the page is set in a mix of roman and italic; the verse is run on as lines within paragraphs. The line "Cocburnum in lucem dedit..." reaches the right edge of the column and may extend into the margin; the word "alendum" is printed beyond the normal measure. The Greek word in "Mnemosyna" is printed in Latin letters in the original ("Mnemosyna") and is copied as printed; the word "vbi" and "Sophia" follow the printer's spelling. Several letters in the scan are damaged or faint, including "laßis" (the long s is printed as ß-like form, copied as printed) and "fenestram"/"fenex" readings near the right edge; "fenestram" in the first line is uncertain and should be checked. Ornament at the foot is a printed fleuron, not text. The heading "Thomæ" is printed as "Thomę" in the scan; copied as Thomæ with doubt. The head "Marco" is the signature of the poem's speaker, set as a paragraph.
